subject: ventures/youtube-chapters-check
professional: a YouTube channel manager / video SEO specialist who also exports markers from Premiere Pro and DaVinci Resolve; first checks: are the three published chapter rules (first timestamp 00:00, at least three ascending timestamps, each chapter at least 10 seconds) applied at their exact boundaries, is the last chapter checked against the video length, does a marker export at the sequence's real frame rate land on the right second, and does the cleaned list keep every chapter the creator wrote

evidence.correctness: The YouTube rules match the live help page (fetched https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9884579 through the proxy, HTTP 200: 'first timestamp you list starts with 00:00 ... at least three timestamps listed in ascending order. The minimum length for video chapters is 10 seconds'). Boundaries recompute right (node scratchpad/yt/probe.mjs): 0:00/0:10/0:20 clean, 0:00/0:09/0:30 flags line 1 under 10 s, two chapters flagged, 0:01 start flagged; last chapter at 2:55 with length 3:04 flagged (9 s), with 3:05 clean. FFMETADATA output for the sample at 1500 s matches ffmpeg-formats 'Metadata' (;FFMETADATA1, [CHAPTER], TIMEBASE=1/1000, START/END ms, = ; # \ escaped); chapters.json matches the Podcasting 2.0 chapters spec v1.2.0 shape. Wrong: frame timecodes at the non-integer rates the page offers (23.976, 29.97) are converted as if timecode seconds were real seconds. Per SMPTE ST 12-1 a non-drop 29.97 timecode 01:00:00:00 is 108,000 frames = 108000 x 1001/30000 = 3603.6 s; the tool returns 3600 (3.6 s early per hour, 10.8 s on a 3-hour stream); 23.976 00:30:00:00 is 1801.8 s, tool 1800. A DaVinci Resolve marker EDL produces chapters titled '001 001 V C 01:00:00:00 ...' at the record-out timecode, not the marker names. WebVTT output writes a title containing '-->' verbatim, which ends the cue per the WebVTT spec.
evidence.completeness: Checked end to end: rule checks with line numbers (pass), duration and last-chapter check (pass), offset shift and drop before 0:00 (pass), optional 0:00 intro (pass), reorder and H:MM:SS normalisation (pass), exact-repeat drop (pass), Premiere tab-separated UTF-16 marker export at 30 fps (pass), Audacity label track with '.' decimals (pass; ',' decimal locales give 'No timestamps found'), chapters.json / FFMETADATA / WebVTT exports (pass), findings CSV (pass), served llms.txt rewritten to marisstella.app (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs youtube-chapters-check: no placeholder origin). Fails: 'convert ... DaVinci ... marker exports' (README.md:6, index.html:59, FAQ index.html:118): Resolve's 'Timeline Markers to EDL' export, the route Resolve offers, yields garbage titles from the event line, ignores the '|M:<name>' line, and the default 01:00:00:00 timeline start makes every chapter fail the 0:00 rule. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/youtube-chapters-check && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 30 tests, 30 pass, ~76 ms. Five seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: MIN_CHAPTERS 3 -> 2 caught; chapter length `< 10` -> `<= 10` SURVIVED (no exactly-10-s test); frame fraction `f / fps` -> `f / 30` SURVIVED; minute/second ceiling `> 59` -> `> 60` SURVIVED (1:60 never tested); first-chapter check `!== 0` -> `> 1` SURVIVED (only 0:45 starts tested). The rule boundaries the product exists to check are untested.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (248 lines), index.html script, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. Pure functions, no network, escaped HTML output, BOM-aware decoding, small and readable. Defects: repair() silently drops lines whose time is impossible (parsed.bad never reaches the change list, calc.mjs:168-200), so the sample broken list loses 'The part everyone gets wrong' with no note; dense regexes (START_RE/END_RE) with no comment on what each separator class is for; range lines '0:00 - 1:30 Intro' become title '1:30 Intro'; duration input that does not parse is silently ignored (index.html options()).
evidence.claims: Backed: the three rules (live help page, quoted above), 'with a line number for every problem' (every rule finding carries a line, the count and mixed-format ones are list-level), 'never uploaded' (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon; index.html has none), 'read from memory ... confirm against the current page' disclosed and now confirmed, disclaimer and non-affiliation on page and README, usage event names match code. Not backed: DaVinci conversion (README.md:6, index.html:59, :118); the fix note 'Anything that cannot be proven is left as it was and named above' (index.html:184) when repair removes an invalid-time line from the cleaned list rather than leaving it; 'set the frame rate to match your sequence' implies 23.976/29.97 sequences convert correctly, they drift 0.1%. The help page names a further cause (active channel strikes or content that may be inappropriate make chapters unavailable) that the 'Why won't my chapters show up?' answer omits; 'Not checked: that YouTube will display the chapters' partly covers it.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a channel manager pastes a description block whose chapters do not show. They get each broken rule with its line, a cleaned list in one format, and a reminder to check the progress bar; for a hand-written list that job is finished in a minute. A Premiere editor on a 30 fps or 25 fps sequence also gets a correct list. Gaps in the first hour: a 29.97/23.976 non-drop sequence puts late chapters seconds early; a Resolve user cannot convert at all; a chapter on an impossible time vanishes from the cleaned copy without notice; the strikes / inappropriate-content cause is not named.
evidence.domain: Against YouTube's published rules (help answer 9884579) the checks are exact and the 0:00, ascending, three and 10-second checks are applied at the right boundaries, including the last chapter when a length is given. Departures: SMPTE ST 12-1 non-drop timecode at 23.976/29.97 counts frames at the nominal 24/30 per labelled second, so seconds = frames x 1001/(nominal x 1000); the tool treats the label as wall time. DaVinci Resolve marker EDLs (CMX3600 events with a '|M:' marker-name comment) are not parsed. WebVTT cue payloads must not contain '-->' (W3C WebVTT, cue text); titles are not sanitised. Codes and formats cited from my own knowledge except the YouTube page, which was fetched.

defects.what: 'Convert DaVinci markers' is claimed on the page, FAQ and README but Resolve's marker EDL export yields chapters titled '001 001 V C 01:00:00:00 ...' at the record-out timecode, ignores the '|M:' marker names, and every chapter fails the 0:00 rule because of the 01:00:00:00 timeline start.
Frame timecodes at 23.976 and 29.97 (non-drop) are treated as wall-clock seconds: 01:00:00:00 at 29.97 NDF returns 3600 s, SMPTE ST 12-1 gives 3603.6 s, so chapters drift 3.6 s per hour of video.

repair() drops lines with an impossible time (11:75) from the cleaned list without listing the drop in changes, while the page says anything unprovable is left as it was; the broken sample loses 'The part everyone gets wrong'.
Rule boundaries are untested: chapter length <= 10, the 59 ceiling, a 0:01 first timestamp and the frame-rate divisor all survive seeded mutation (4 of 5 mutants survived).
WebVTT export writes titles verbatim, so a title containing '-->' ends the cue (WebVTT forbids '-->' in cue payloads).
Range lines '0:00 - 1:30 Intro' produce the title '1:30 Intro'; Audacity labels with comma decimals give 'No timestamps found'.
The 'Why won't my chapters show up?' answer omits the cause YouTube's help page names besides list format: active channel strikes or content that may be inappropriate make chapters unavailable.
Without a video length the last chapter's 10-second rule is skipped with no info finding saying so; an unparseable length is silently ignored.

verdict: The YouTube half is right: the 00:00, three-ascending and 10-second rules match the live help page word for word, the boundaries recompute exactly (10 s passes, 9 s fails, the last chapter checked against the length), and the FFMETADATA and chapters.json exports match their specs. It misses the bar on the converter half and on its tests. DaVinci conversion is claimed in three places and does not work: a Resolve marker EDL yields event-line garbage as titles. Frame timecodes at 23.976 and 29.97 non-drop are read as wall time, 3.6 s early per hour (3600 vs SMPTE 3603.6). The cleaned list silently drops a line with an impossible time despite saying it leaves such lines alone. Four of five seeded boundary mutants survive 30 tests. A channel manager fixing a hand-typed description list can rely on it; an editor converting Resolve or 29.97 markers cannot.
